title: Seat exits are classified from real provider lines: limit roster, bounded output tail, durable pause ledger
description:
SPIDR child 1 of task-2723a9b400984ab7b1b10f97c3523c81 (leaf; no sibling dependency). Filed by architect-16a01670 2026-09-04, measured at main 68eb1c5d.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: three PURE modules under apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/ with their tests. No spawner, wrapper, read or UI change (children 2-3).

MEASURED (re-measure before planning):
- The spawner starts the seat with `stdio: ["pipe", "inherit", "inherit"]` (apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawner.ts:157) - stdout/stderr are inherited, nothing is captured, and the exit is reported as `AgentProcessFailureError(reason, exitCode, signal)` (:196-204) with only `[wrapper] <item> agent exited <code>` logged (:314). agent-spawner.ts is 417 lines (already over the 400 hard cap): the tee + tail logic must live in a new module so child 2's spawner edit stays minimal.
- Durable records the wrapper writes without a registry kind: `recordPublishReceipt` (apps/daemon/src/repository/publish-ledger.ts:173 `commandKind: PUBLISH_RECEIPT_COMMAND_KIND = "internal.repository.publish_receipt"`, publish-receipt-contracts.ts:17) and the verifier receipt (review/verifier-receipt-ledger.ts:138, "internal.integration.verifier_receipt") commit through `store.commitExpectedVersionDecision` with an internal kind and a daemon principal id (NODE_PUBLISHER_PRINCIPAL_ID = "daemon:node-publisher") - the same pattern serves the seat-exit receipt and the provider pause.
- Real limit lines to quote verbatim in fixtures: the claude session-limit line recorded 2026-09-03 21:04 local (memory productize-loop-2026-09-03: "You've hit your session limit · resets 12:10am Asia/Jerusalem"), the codex quota refusal (memory: exhausted until 2026-09-08) - pull the exact bytes from D:/projexts/UnAI/.moe-next/wrapper.log (or the scratchpad drive logs) and from a fresh `claude -p` / `codex exec` refusal if reachable; never invent a line. The seat's provider = `providerFor(command)` (orchestrator/moe-up-credentials.ts:143; leaf "claude" | "codex").

FEATURE: (1) `seat-exit-classifier.ts`: `classifySeatExit({ provider, exitCode, signal, tail: readonly string[] }) -> { kind: "COMPLETED" | "FAILED" | "PROVIDER_LIMIT", resetAt: string | null, lastLine: string | null, matched: string | null }`; exit 0 -> COMPLETED; otherwise the tail (last 40 lines) is scanned against a FROZEN per-provider roster of patterns, each entry carrying the verbatim sample line it was written from and an optional reset-instant parser (claude "resets 12:10am Asia/Jerusalem" -> the next such wall-clock instant in that zone from the exit time, ISO; codex "until 2026-09-08" -> that date at 00:00Z); no match -> FAILED (never guessed); the roster is exported so a bidirectional test can enumerate it. (2) `seat-output-tail.ts`: `createOutputTail(limitLines = 40, limitBytes = 16 KiB)` with `push(chunk: Buffer|string)` splitting lines, keeping the last N, and `lines()`; pure, no process access - child 2 tees the seat's piped stdout/stderr into it while still writing them to the wrapper's own stdout/stderr byte-for-byte. (3) `provider-pause-ledger.ts`: `recordSeatExit(store, input)` -> `moe-seat-exit/1` {sessionId, workItemId, provider, kind, resetAt, lastLine, exitCode, decidedAt} and `recordProviderPause(store, input)` -> `moe-provider-pause/1` {provider, resetAt, since, cause: {workItemId, lastLine}} on aggregate `provider-pause:<projectId>:<provider>` with internal kinds "internal.wrapper.seat_exit" / "internal.wrapper.provider_pause" and principal "daemon:agent-wrapper"; `readProviderPause(store, projectId, provider, now)` -> the latest pause when `resetAt > now`, else null; `clearProviderPause` is a record with resetAt = now (the same event type, so a read at or after it answers null).
definitionOfDone: Classifier test with VERBATIM fixture lines (each fixture cites where it was captured): at least three claude limit lines (session limit with a wall-clock reset, usage limit, rate limit) and one codex quota line classify PROVIDER_LIMIT with the parsed `resetAt` (or null when the line carries no instant), and `matched` names the roster entry; an ordinary stack trace, an ENOENT, and exit 0 classify FAILED/FAILED/COMPLETED; a bidirectional arm asserts every roster entry is matched by its own sample line and every sample line matches exactly one entry.

Reset parsing pinned: '12:10am Asia/Jerusalem' from an exit at 2026-09-03T18:04:00Z resolves to 2026-09-03T21:10:00Z (next occurrence in that zone), and an exit AFTER that wall-clock time resolves to the following day; a date-only codex line resolves to that date 00:00:00Z; an unparseable instant yields resetAt null with kind still PROVIDER_LIMIT.

Output tail test: 100 pushed lines keep the last 40; a 64 KiB single chunk keeps the last 16 KiB split on newlines; CRLF and partial trailing lines handled; no unbounded growth (assert the internal buffer length).

Pause ledger test over a REAL store: recordProviderPause then readProviderPause(now < resetAt) returns it, (now >= resetAt) returns null, a later record with resetAt = now clears it; recordSeatExit writes an exact-key `moe-seat-exit/1` decision under principal daemon:agent-wrapper readable by decision kind; both internal kinds are absent from the daemon command registry and MCP allowlist (roster tests unchanged, count lines quoted).
Gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`; each new production module <= 250 lines with its `.js` bridge (`wc -l` quoted).
taskRails: NEVER GUESS A LIMIT: the roster is built only from verbatim provider lines with their capture source cited in the fixture; anything unmatched is FAILED.
PURE LEAF: no spawner, wrapper, read-route or UI change; internal record kinds ride commitExpectedVersionDecision like the publish/verifier receipts and never enter the command registry.
Refusals/kinds assert exact values; mutate to prove each arm red (global rail 1). <=250 lines per production source, hard stop 400.

5 fixtures / 5 roster ids: claude/session-limit (LIVE 2026-09-03 21:04 seat #4 exit 1, memory productize-loop-2026-09-03, template corroborated), claude/usage-limit, claude/weekly-limit, claude/rate-limit (all BINARY), codex/usage-limit (LIVE today).

Cross-provider collision found at design time: codex's line contains "You've hit your usage limit" too, so a naive claude pattern would also match it. Measured discriminator: claude's H0 never emits a period after the limit name (suffix is "", " \xB7 resets X", " \xB7 progress saved" or " \xB7 contact your admin to increase it"); codex's sentence always does ("usage limit. Visit"). Claude patterns therefore carry a negative lookahead so the bidirectional arm can assert GLOBAL exactly-one-entry, not merely per-provider.

ROSTER IDS: claude/session-limit, claude/usage-limit, claude/weekly-limit, claude/rate-limit, codex/usage-limit.

PATTERNS (each a whole provider SENTENCE, never a bare /limit/):
  /You've hit your session limit(?![.\w])/iu
  /You've hit your usage limit(?![.\w])/iu
  /You've hit your weekly limit(?![.\w])/iu
  /Fast limit reached and temporarily disabled/iu
  /hit your usage limit\.\s+Visit https:\/\/chatgpt\.com\/codex/iu
The `(?![.\w])` is not decoration: codex's live refusal contains the literal clause "You've hit your usage limit." so a naive claude pattern matches it too. Measured discriminator — claude's H0 composer never emits a period after the limit name (suffix is "", " \xB7 resets X", " \xB7 progress saved", " \xB7 contact your admin to increase it") while codex's sentence always does. With the lookahead, the bidirectional arm asserts GLOBAL exactly-one-entry (`SEAT_EXIT_ROSTER.filter(o => o.pattern.test(entry.sample))` === [entry.id]), not merely per-provider.

RESET PARSING — three real forms, tried in order:
  1. CLAUDE_WALL_CLOCK `(?:(Mon) (D),\s*)?(H):(MM)\s*(am|pm)\s+\(?(Zone/Id)\)?` — parens OPTIONAL because the 2026-09-03 capture rendered the zone bare and 2.1.260 parenthesises it. Both are real bytes.
  2. CODEX_DATED `(Mon) (D)(st|nd|rd|th)?, (YYYY) (H):(MM) (AM|PM)` -> resolved in UTC.
  3. ISO_DATE `YYYY-MM-DD` -> that date 00:00:00.000Z (satisfies the DoD's date-only clause; NO roster entry uses it, because no provider was observed printing that form).
Zone math: `Intl.DateTimeFormat(... hourCycle:"h23", timeZone ...).formatToParts` gives the zone's fields; offset = Date.UTC(fields) - instant. TWO PASSES (offset read at the naive guess, then re-read at the instant that guess resolved to) so a reset on the far side of a DST change converts with ITS OWN offset. Zone validated by `Intl.supportedValuesOf("timeZone")` with a `new Intl.DateTimeFormat({timeZone})` try/catch fallback for an engine lacking the method.
Roll-forward: bare wall clock -> today's occurrence in that zone, else tomorrow's. Dated-without-year -> the exit's local year, else +1 year (the renderer omits the year only while it equals the current one).

CODEX ZONE CAVEAT (documented in the module, not papered over): codex prints its reset in the HOST's local wall clock with NO zone. Reading it as UTC is deliberate and conservative — for any zone east of UTC it moves the instant LATER, so the pause outlasts the limit instead of expiring early into another refusal.

implementationPlan.description: OUTPUT TAIL (test first, then module). apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/seat-output-tail.test.ts then seat-output-tail.ts (+ .js bridge). `createOutputTail(options?: { maxLines?: number; maxBytes?: number })` (defaults 40 / 16384) -> `{ push(chunk: Buffer | string): void; lines(): readonly string[]; bytes(): number }`: chunks are decoded as UTF-8 with a streaming decoder (a multi-byte sequence split across chunks must not corrupt - use `new TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: false })` with `stream: true`), split on \n with \r stripped, a partial trailing line kept until the next chunk or `lines()`; keep at most maxLines entries and at most maxBytes total (drop oldest first); `lines()` returns a frozen copy. Arms: 100 lines -> last 40 in order; one 64 KiB chunk -> the retained lines total <= 16384 bytes and end with the chunk's last line; CRLF input -> no \r in lines; a chunk ending mid-line then a chunk completing it -> one joined line; a UTF-8 sequence split across two pushes -> the character intact; `bytes()` never exceeds maxBytes after any push (property-style loop over random chunk sizes with a seeded PRNG). Run the file: green, count line quoted.
implementationPlan.note:
OUTPUT TAIL — test first (RED: "Cannot find module './seat-output-tail.js'", `Test Files 1 failed (1) / Tests no tests`), then module. GREEN: `Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 10 passed (10)`.

API: `createOutputTail(options?: { maxBytes?: number; maxLines?: number })` (defaults 16384 / 40) -> `{ bytes(): number; lines(): readonly string[]; push(chunk: Buffer | string): void }`. `lines()` returns a FROZEN copy including any partial trailing line; `bytes()` is the byte width of exactly the lines `lines()` would return (newline separators are NOT counted, and maxBytes bounds that same quantity — one definition, no second unit to get wrong).

BOUND ORDER, deliberate and pinned by an arm: line cap first, then byte cap, then head-truncation of a lone survivor. `enforce()` stops dropping at ONE remaining entry and truncates it to its last maxBytes instead — a provider's refusal sentence trails the noise, so keeping a long line's TAIL beats dropping the line. Enforcement runs PER LINE inside push(), not once per chunk, so a 64 KiB chunk never materialises every line it carries before the bounds apply.

TWO PLANNED ARM EXPECTATIONS WERE WRONG AS I FIRST WROTE THEM AND WERE CORRECTED AGAINST THE MEASURED SEMANTICS, not the other way round:
 - 64 KiB arm: my first version used 2048 short lines, which the 40-LINE cap alone satisfies — the byte bound would never have been exercised and the arm would have been vacuous for its own title. Rewritten to 64 lines x 1023 bytes (`Buffer.byteLength(chunk+"\n") === 65536` asserted, so the "64 KiB" in the title is measured, not claimed): under the line cap, so the BYTE bound does the work — 16384/1023 leaves exactly 16 lines. Asserts length 16, `bytes() === 16*1023`, first retained line starts "0048", last "0063".
 - explicit-bounds arm: `{maxBytes: 12, maxLines: 3}` on "aaaa\nbbbb\ncccc\ndddd\n" retains 12 bytes, which is <= 12, so my expected ["cccc","dddd"] was arithmetically impossible. Changed to maxBytes 11 (drops to ["cccc","dddd"], bytes 8) and ADDED a second tail at maxBytes 1024 proving the line cap alone yields ["bbbb","cccc","dddd"] — the two bounds are now separated, not conflated.

OTHER ARMS: 100 lines -> last 40, `lines[0]==="line 60"`, `lines[39]==="line 99"`; a single 1,000,000-char line -> exactly 1 line, length <= 16384, `endsWith("y")` (tail kept, no hang); CRLF -> no "\r" in any line; "You've hit your ses" + "sion limit\n" -> one joined line, and the partial is readable BEFORE its newline arrives (a seat killed mid-line still yields its last words); a UTF-8 sequence split across two pushes (`Buffer.indexOf(0xC2)+1` on "resets 12:10am · done") -> the middle dot intact, no U+FFFD (one `TextDecoder("utf-8",{fatal:false})` lives for the tail's life and holds the continuation via `stream: true`); string and Buffer pushes interchangeable; the frozen snapshot from `lines()` is unaffected by a later push; property loop of 400 seeded-PRNG (mulberry32, seed 0x5EA7) chunks of 1..900 chars with ~8% newlines asserting both bounds after EVERY push — and asserting `pushes === 400` plus a non-empty tail at the end, so a sweep that generated zero cases could not pass.
